targetArchitecture.runtime: Browser -> Vercel -> Firebase Auth token -> Render EOS API -> EOS authorization -> PostgreSQL
targetArchitecture.principle: Firebase is permitted only for sign-in identity and Firebase UID correlation to an EOS Principal/Employee. All business data, business authorization, and business transport must run through the Render EOS API against PostgreSQL, not through Firestore or Firebase Functions.

IDENTITY_ONLY.description: Firebase usage that establishes or verifies who the caller is (sign-in, ID token verification, custom-claims issuance) or correlates a Firebase UID to an EOS Principal/Employee. This is outside the BUSINESS_RUNTIME ratchet for the current business-runtime exit phase; eventual identity/auth migration is a separate future Firebase-exit concern, not decided here. RECLASSIFIED 2026-09-29 (Controller ruling EOS IDENTITY BOUNDARY): Firebase Authentication is a TRANSITIONAL ACTIVE dependency pending retirement, not a permanent carve-out -- see exitLedger FX-AUTH-001.

exitLedger.responsibility: Firebase Authentication: browser sign-in (firebase/auth), ID-token verification in the EOS API (firebase-admin lazy import in functions/src/eosApi/server.ts) and in Firebase Functions, custom-claims issuance, and Firebase UID correlation to an EOS Principal (principals.identity_provider='firebase').
exitLedger.ruling: Controller ruling 2026-09-29, EOS IDENTITY BOUNDARY (Option A refined): Firebase Auth is an active Firebase EXIT item, retired only later with separate authorization. Supersedes 'firebaseAllowedAfterExit'.
exitLedger.eosOwner: EOS identity/session foundation: eos_policy.principal_identities (migration 1764200000000), functions/src/eosAuth/*, field-ops-app-vite/src/auth/eosSession.js
exitLedger.replacementState: BUILT_LOCAL_INERT: additive EOS access token + verifier + binding + nonprod persona issuer; Firebase sign-in unchanged
exitLedger.countRule: The IDENTITY_ONLY file sets may not grow. They are not yet fenced by scripts/firebaseExitGuard.mjs; functions/test/eosAuthNoFirebase.test.mjs pins the total at 7 and fails on any increase.
exitLedger.removalCondition: Every human and harness session is EOS-issued (a separately authorized human front door exists), every EOS API request verifies an EOS token, no transport requires a Firebase ID token, and the Firebase Functions callables that verify Firebase tokens are retired; then firebase/auth, firebase-admin auth verification and the firebase primary bindings are removed under separate authorization.

BUSINESS_RUNTIME.description: Firebase usage that transports, persists, authorizes, or executes EOS business logic: Firestore reads/writes, Firebase Functions callables/triggers, and firebase-admin Firestore persistence. Must trend to zero per the architecture ruling. The four classes are fenced at EVERY business-runtime root -- field-ops-app-vite/src, functions/src and integrations -- which is twelve keys, not four: a dependency class does not stop being a Firebase business-runtime dependency because of which directory it appears in. Eight of the twelve are empty today and are ratchets pinned at zero, so any entry at all in them is an immediate violation rather than a baseline row to add. Each class is fenced in BOTH its source shapes: the subpath specifier (firebase-admin/firestore, firebase/firestore, and their compat builds) AND the namespace form -- a bare package-root import (firebase-admin, firebase, firebase/app) together with a Firestore/Functions access expression in a comment- and string-blanked view of the source. The namespace form names no forbidden specifier and was a confirmed live bypass at main 64008d5ae0bdd9532909671b15a91122400accf1 until it was closed; the conjunction with an access expression is what preserves the IDENTITY_ONLY carve-out, since importing the firebase-admin root for app().auth().verifyIdToken() is not the violation. A Firestore handle RE-EXPORTED from one module is outside this direct-import fence by construction; the growth of those transitional shims' consumer sets is governed separately by scripts/firebaseShimBoundary.mjs against docs/architecture/firebase-shim-consumer-census.json, under the Owner ruling that the shims may remain temporarily and their existing consumers are not violations.

migrationStates.NOT_STARTED: No Render EOS API / PostgreSQL equivalent exists yet for this dependency.
migrationStates.DUAL_READ_TEST: A Render EOS API / PostgreSQL equivalent exists and is being verified against the Firebase path; Firebase remains the system of record.
migrationStates.READY: The Render EOS API / PostgreSQL equivalent has passed verification and cutover is authorized but not yet performed.
migrationStates.CUTOVER: The Render EOS API / PostgreSQL path is the system of record; the Firebase path is inert in the live runtime.
migrationStates.RETIRED: The Firebase business dependency has been removed from source and from the baseline.

dispositions.IDENTITY_ONLY: This dependency is sign-in identity or UID correlation and is outside this business-runtime ratchet for the current exit phase; identity/auth migration, if any, is a separate future Firebase-exit concern. Since 2026-09-29 this is TRANSITIONAL: Firebase Authentication is an active exit item (FX-AUTH-001) whose EOS replacement is docs/architecture/eos-identity-session-foundation.md; retirement requires separate authorization.
dispositions.MIGRATE_TO_POSTGRES_RENDER: This dependency has (or will have) a live EOS business equivalent and must be re-pointed to the Render EOS API / PostgreSQL.
dispositions.ARCHIVE: This dependency serves data with no ongoing live business need; it is captured as read-only evidence/history rather than migrated forward.
dispositions.RETIRE: This dependency has no ongoing purpose and is deleted rather than migrated.

ratchet.rule: For every baselineKey listed under classification.BUSINESS_RUNTIME.baselineKeys, the set of live-runtime files depending on it may only shrink relative to docs/architecture/firebase-exit-baseline.json. It may never grow. A file already in the baseline for a given key is temporarily tolerated so migration can proceed incrementally; a file NOT in the baseline for that key introducing that dependency is a new violation.

domainMigrationWaveModel.description: Each baseline file belongs to exactly one domain: the first path segment beneath field-ops-app-vite/src or functions/src (for example functions/src/cycleCount/cycleCountCallables.ts belongs to domain 'cycleCount'). A migration wave groups one or more domains that move to the Render EOS API / PostgreSQL together. This manifest defines the model only -- it does not assign domains to waves, order waves, or assert a disposition per domain, because that scheduling decision belongs to the engineers and owners doing the migration work, not to this control document. Once a wave is scheduled, it is recorded here as an entry below with the domain names, its disposition (one of the values in `dispositions`), and its migrationState (one of the values in `migrationStates`).
